# How to Create AI-Generated Podcast Show Notes in 2026

Show notes are what make a podcast discoverable and reusable, yet most creators skip them. The decision is whether you want a full transcript-to-notes pipeline or a quick summary from a chat model. Either way, the bottleneck is clean transcription—everything else builds on it.

## The tools worth considering

The following tools cover different parts of the job. Each section notes what it is for, where it helps, its strengths, and its honest limits so you can judge fit before signing up.

## Whisper

Whisper Whisper is OpenAI's open-source speech-to-text model.

For podcast show notes, it helps with subtitle generation: Produce timestamped captions for videos in dozens of languages

Strengths:
- Free to run locally with no per-minute transcription fees
- Transcribes 90+ languages including many low-resource ones

Honest limits:
- Larger models need substantial GPU memory to run comfortably
- May require a VPN in some regions to access hosted APIs
- Access may require a VPN in some regions

[[link:/tools/11|Whisper]] works best for content creation.

## Descript

Descript Descript is an audio and video editor built around the transcript: editing the text cuts the audio.

For podcast show notes, it helps with podcast editing: Remove filler words and polish episodes through transcript edits

Strengths:
- Transcript-based editing makes audio work accessible to non-editors
- Voice cloning enables overdubs without re-recording whole passages

Honest limits:
- Some users need a VPN to access the service reliably
- Complex music or multitrack editing may suit traditional DAWs better
- Access may require a VPN in some regions

[[link:/tools/79|Descript]] works best for teams.

## Notta AI

Notta AI Notta is an AI transcription and note-taking tool that converts audio recordings into searchable text.

For podcast show notes, it helps with transcribe meetings: Turn recorded calls into searchable text with speaker labels

Strengths:
- Wide language support suits teams with international participants
- Speaker identification keeps transcripts readable with multiple people talking

Honest limits:
- Accuracy depends on audio quality, accents, and background noise
- Longer recordings need a paid plan for extended transcription volume

[[link:/tools/485|Notta AI]] works best for teams.

## Adobe Podcast AI

Adobe Podcast AI Adobe Podcast AI is a browser-based audio enhancement service for podcasters, YouTubers and interviewers recording on ordinary microphones.

For podcast show notes, it helps with podcast cleanup: Remove room noise and echo from interview recordings before publishing

Strengths:
- Cloud-based enhancement works entirely in the browser without extra software
- Removes noise and echo effectively, noticeably improving cheap microphone recordings

Honest limits:
- Free tier limits upload length, so long episodes need a paid plan
- Cloud processing requires uploading audio, which may not suit sensitive recordings

[[link:/tools/1535|Adobe Podcast AI]] works best for podcasters.

## ElevenLabs

ElevenLabs ElevenLabs is an AI voice platform for generating lifelike speech and cloning voices.

For podcast show notes, it helps with audiobook narration: Produce full-length audiobooks with consistent narration voices across chapters

Strengths:
- Voice quality and emotional range are among the best available today
- Instant cloning needs only short samples to capture a speaker's tone

Honest limits:
- Free tier is limited; serious production requires a paid plan
- Access requires a VPN in some regions, complicating consistent use
- Access may require a VPN in some regions

[[link:/tools/8|ElevenLabs]] works best for professionals.

## Auphonic

Auphonic Auphonic is an AI post-production service for podcasts and audio creators.

For podcast show notes, it helps with podcast polish: Automatically level, denoise and polish episodes before publishing

Strengths:
- Automatic levelling and noise removal reduce hours of manual mixing
- Handles loudness normalisation, important for podcast platform compliance

Honest limits:
- Free tier caps processing time per month for longer episodes
- Cloud processing means uploading audio before hearing any results

[[link:/tools/225|Auphonic]] works best for podcasting.

## Podcastle

Podcastle Podcastle is an AI-powered podcast production platform covering the full workflow: remote recording with cloud backup, AI-assisted audio editing and cleanup, text-to-speech voiceover and tools for publishing episodes.

For podcast show notes, it helps with remote recording: Capture interviews with guests joining from anywhere online

Strengths:
- Covers recording, editing and publishing in one browser workspace
- Remote recording captures each speaker's track separately

Honest limits:
- Heavy editing sessions can strain older computers and browsers
- Free tier caps recording time and advanced AI features

[[link:/tools/228|Podcastle]] works best for podcasting.

## ChatGPT

ChatGPT ChatGPT is OpenAI's general-purpose conversational assistant used for writing, analysis, coding, brainstorming, and everyday questions.

For podcast show notes, it helps with drafting documents: Write emails, reports, and outlines with editing help at every step

Strengths:
- Handles text, images, files, and voice in one conversational interface
- Free tier provides generous everyday access without requiring a credit card

Honest limits:
- Service is unavailable in some countries and often needs a VPN
- Answers can contain confident-sounding errors that require fact-checking before use
- Access may require a VPN in some regions

[[link:/tools/6|ChatGPT]] works best for beginners.

## Claude

Claude Claude is Anthropic's assistant built for long documents, writing and analysis.

For podcast show notes, it helps with long document review: Analyze entire manuscripts and codebases in one conversation

Strengths:
- Large context window handles lengthy documents without splitting them
- Projects keep related work organized with persistent context

Honest limits:
- May require a VPN for access in some regions
- Free tier usage limits push heavy users toward paid plans
- Access may require a VPN in some regions

[[link:/tools/20|Claude]] works best for professionals.

## How to choose

- Need a transcript first? Whisper (open source) or Descript.
- Want notes generated from the transcript? ChatGPT or Claude.
- Prefer an all-in-one? Notta AI or Adobe Podcast AI transcribe and summarize.
- Decide how much editing you'll do; AI drafts still need a human pass.
- Publish notes everywhere—your site, newsletter, and episode page.

## A chaining workflow that works

Transcribe with [[link:/tools/11|Whisper]] or [[link:/tools/79|Descript]], paste the transcript into [[link:/tools/6|ChatGPT]] with a notes prompt, then clean and format before publishing to your site and newsletter.

## Common mistakes

- Publishing raw AI notes with timestamp errors and misattributed quotes.
- Skipping transcription and trying to summarize from memory.
- Forgetting links and resources mentioned in the episode.
- Leaving notes unformatted—a wall of text nobody reads.

## FAQ

### What's the easiest way to make podcast show notes?

Transcribe with Whisper or Descript, then ask ChatGPT or Claude to turn the transcript into timestamped notes with a prompt.

### Is Whisper free?

Yes, Whisper is open source and free to run, making it a strong starting point for transcription.

### Can one tool do it all?

Notta AI and Adobe Podcast AI transcribe and summarize, but a quick human edit still improves the result.

### How long should show notes be?

A short summary, three to five timestamps, and a resource list is enough for most episodes.

The right pick depends on your starting point and constraints, not on which tool tops a list. Start with one job, learn the tool, and expand only when the payoff is clear.
tldr: Transcribe first with Whisper or Descript, then have ChatGPT or Claude structure the notes—always edit before publishing.
